subject: Post-demo: action items for latency & concurrency decisioning
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@alpine.ai>, Maya Lopez <maya@alpine.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: action items for latency & concurrency decisioning

Hi Samir / Maya — thanks again for taking the time to demo Alpine's streaming inference use case today. Quick recap and a proposed checklist so we can align on acceptance criteria and next steps.

TL;DR (ask): please confirm the target latency/throughput numbers below and whether the procurement timeline (~6 weeks) is accurate so we can lock the mutual action plan (MAP).

What we observed during the demo:
- Streaming requires partial-response emission every 120–150ms for your UI to feel "live".
- p95 end-to-end token latency in our test harness (US-west) was ~230ms on the baseline model variant with default batching.
- Concurrent sustained QPS target you mentioned: 100 QPS with 2x burst to 300 for promo windows.

Proposed SLO checklist (for alignment) — please confirm accept/reject or adjust:
1) Latency: p95 <= 200ms for interactive streaming in US-west (goal). If not achievable initially, p95 <= 250ms acceptable for phase 1.
2) Concurrency/throughput: support sustained 100 QPS with autoscale margin to handle 300 QPS bursts.
3) Streaming behavior: partial-chunk granularity <= 150ms, support for chunked token streaming and finalization markers.
4) Fallback: automated fallback to smaller quantized model when backend queueing > 500ms.
5) Observability: per-request token / latency traces and per-route cost breakdown enabled (30d retention).

Attachments: redwood_slo_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with acceptance criteria + perf test plan).

Next steps proposed:
- You: confirm targets and procurement timeline (procurement@alpine.ai) — by Thu EOD if possible.
- Us (Rishi): share a canary plan (Dedicated vs hosted) and resource estimate.
- Us (Ben): share a draft MAP PDF and runbook for the POC canary.

Suggested date for a short follow-up (40 min) to finalize acceptance criteria: Thu 22 Oct, 09:00–09:40 PT. I’ll send a calendar invite once we have confirmation.

Thanks — Stephanie

--

From: Samir Khan <samir@alpine.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Lopez <maya@alpine.ai>, procurement@alpine.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: action items for latency & concurrency decisioning

Thanks Stephanie — great recap. I looped in Maya and procurement. A few clarifications from our side and confirmation on timelines.

Confirmations / clarifications:
- Latency: our product team would like p95 <= 250ms for phase 1 (US), with a stretch to 200ms. We can commit to the 200ms goal as a conditional SLA if the canary shows consistent results.
- Throughput: sustained 100 QPS is correct for our baseline traffic (peak campaign windows see ~250–300 QPS for ~15 minutes).
- Streaming: chunking <= 150ms is required to satisfy our front-end UX.
- Fallback: agree with auto-fallback to a quantized 4-bit variant, but need to understand quality deltas (we'll need example outputs).

Procurement timeline: procurement@alpine.ai indicates ~6 weeks for vendor sign-off + PO after contract redlines. We can push for 4 weeks if legal gets the draft quickly.

Two small asks: 
1) Can you confirm whether KV cache warmup will reduce token cost by ~20% (as mentioned in the demo)? We need an estimate for monthly cost modeling.
2) Please share the network diagram / recommended egress ports for our infra team (attached).

Attached: alpine_network_diagram.pdf

Happy to join Thu 22 Oct 09:00 PT — confirming our side.

—Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform, Alpine.ai
samir@alpine.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: canary / capacity thoughts (do not forward)

Stephanie / Rishi — quick internal note following Samir's answers.

- If phase 1 accepts p95 <= 250ms with stretch to 200ms, we should propose a Dedicated canary (8x A10G or equivalent) to hit consistent p95 numbers. Hosted may work but makes SLA commitments harder.
- For burst handling to 300 QPS, plan: autoscale policy with 2x burst nodes + pre-warming 1 node 10 minutes before campaign window (we'll add webhooks for schedule-based prewarm).
- KV cache: expect 15–25% token reduction after steady-state warmup; I'll confirm with infra bench and add the exact math to the MAP.

I will draft the canary resource estimate and add owners. Rishi — can you pull our recent benchmark numbers (p95 vs batch size) so we have a concrete table?

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Thanks all — I’ve updated the MAP and attached a PDF with owners, acceptance criteria, and the runbook for the canary: MAP-alpine-20261020.pdf. Key points below.

Finalized acceptance criteria (phase 1):
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms across US-west (goal: 200ms).
- Throughput: sustained 100 QPS; handle 300 QPS bursts with autoscale and prewarm.
- Streaming: chunk <= 150ms and include finalization token marker.
- Regression: end-to-end quality regression <= 2% (WPS) when switching to quantized fallback.

Owners & timeline:
- Redwood AE (Stephanie): MAP owner, coordinate legal/contract handoff — target: share contract draft by 2026-11-05.
- Redwood SE (Ben): canary design and resource estimate — deliverable: canary runbook by 2026-10-28.
- Redwood Infra (Rishi): benchmark matrix + KV-cache savings estimate — deliverable: bench results by 2026-10-26.
- Alpine (Samir/Maya): confirm procurement timing and sign PO — target: PO issued by 2026-11-15.

Action items (short):
1) Rishi: bench numbers for p95 vs batch size + KV savings (due Mon 10/26).
2) Ben: canary resource estimate + runbook (due Wed 10/28).
3) Stephanie: circulate contract draft and finalize SOW (target 11/05).
4) Samir/Procurement: confirm PO timeline and legal redline turnaround (please reply with a target).

We’ll use the Thu 22 Oct slot for a 40-min alignment to walk the MAP and sign off on owners — invite sent. If anything changes, flag here.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.
